title: Don’t put all your eggs in one basket
desc: Why spreading money limits the damage from one bad pick

cards.title: One bad day
cards.situation: Ben puts $10,000 into one company. Max puts $1,000 into each of 10 companies, including Ben’s. That company falls 50%. How much does each lose?

visual.label: Ben holds one stock; Max holds ten equal stocks

options.feedback: The company fell 50% for both. But Max only had a tenth of his money in it.
Same crash, a tenth of the damage. That’s diversification.

options.text: Max loses more: he owns more stocks
options.feedback: Owning more stocks doesn’t add to this loss. Only one company fell, and Max had just $1,000 in it.

cards.added: Feedback for C written for the Academy

cards.title: Spread the risk
cards.text: **[[diversification|Diversification]]** means spreading money across many holdings. One bad pick then hurts a little, not a lot.

visual.label: After the drop Ben has $5,000 left; Max has $9,500

blocks.tip: Single stocks can and do fall 50% or more, sometimes in a day. Spreading out limits the damage from any one.

cards.title: One bad apple
cards.text: One company hits trouble and its stock halves. In a 10-stock portfolio, the other nine rose about 7%, so the whole portfolio still ended about +1%.

items.title: One year
items.label: Over one year the single stock falls 50% while the 10-stock portfolio ends about 1% higher

cards.foot: Diversification cuts the damage from one company. It can’t stop the whole market from falling.

cards.title: Count the damage
cards.q: You own 5 stocks, $2,000 in each: $10,000 in all. One of them falls 50%. How much do you lose?

visual.label: Five equal holdings of $2,000; one falls

options.feedback: Only one holding fell, and it was a fifth of your money.
One holding of $2,000 lost half. The other four didn’t move, so the damage stays small.
$2,000 is the whole holding. It fell by half, not to zero.
That’s too small. Take half of the $2,000 that fell.

cards.added: Feedback for the options the board doesn’t show written for the Academy

cards.title: What it protects

options.feedback: Spreading out shrinks the hit from one company. Bad news there touches only a small part of your money.

options.text: A crash in the whole market
options.feedback: When the whole market falls, most stocks fall with it. Spreading across stocks can’t stop that.
Spreading out shrinks the hit from one company. When the whole market falls, most stocks fall with it.
Diversifying doesn’t cut fees. It limits how much one bad pick can hurt you.

cards.headline: You know why one basket is risky.
lines: One stock can fall 50% or more.
Spread money so one bad pick hurts a little.
Diversifying can’t stop a whole-market fall.
